title: command_class keeps any word after git, gh, claude and the other subcommand tools, so a prompt's or an argument's first word can reach a committed call row
goal: kbusage.command_class names a SUBCOMMANDS tool's subcommand only from a per-tool allowlist of real subcommands (git status, gh pr, glab mr, uv run ...) and else the tool alone, so no free word of a prompt or an argument reaches a call.tool row or a repeats story; a planted 'claude -p hello' and 'gh secretword' give 'claude' and 'gh'. Found by the SP-smqwmchu review.

run: import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'_tools');import kbusage as k;sys.exit(1 if k.command_class('claude -p hello') == 'claude.hello' or k.command_class('gh secretword') == 'gh.secretword' else 0)
